guard.notes: Kimi Code has no project-level hook file: .kimi/config.toml holds the [[hooks]] entries (PreToolUse, matcher Bash|Write|Edit|Read|Grep|Glob) and the user mirrors them into ~/.kimi-code/config.toml. Hooks run with cwd set to the session's project directory, so the relative guard path works once mirrored; exit 2 blocks the call. Until the mirror exists the policy is honoured behaviourally - pipe a doubtful call through the guard before running it.

capabilitiesNotes: toolEvents: this file's own guard.notes already record the confirmed fact - "There is no project hook, so the policy in tooling/agentos/agent-hooks is honoured behaviourally" - no vendor adapter and no PreToolUse mechanism exists in this repository for Kimi, matching hooksSupport: behavioral. The other five: permissions.notes below already says the runtime is not configured, and no script, doc or event log here has ever exercised a Kimi subagent, resume, cancel, usage report or worktree-aware run - left unknown rather than assumed from the product's general reputation. Updated 2026-09-30: .kimi/config.toml now exists as the mirror-source for ~/.kimi-code/config.toml; toolEvents stays `unsupported` until the user mirrors it and a run is exercised, then re-grade.
pricingNotes: No rates are recorded for this vendor; `delivery estimate --runtime kimi` warns and falls back to the placeholder table.

permissions.notes: At first launch in Kimi: ask the user to mirror .kimi/config.toml into ~/.kimi-code/config.toml, and ask for the model mapping and how approvals are granted. Structural changes to roles, agents or skills always need explicit user approval, in every mode.
